8876171.twitter_share_message: “Gifford suggests “Stephen’s witticism implies that Mr. Deasy’s letter is addressed to a chosen p…” —@Genius

children: Gifford suggests “Stephen’s witticism implies that Mr. Deasy’s letter is addressed to a chosen people in a promised land,” which would certainly be consistent with the references to “mouth” and “foot”, considering the letter’s subject having to do with Foot and Mouth Disease. However, if one considers the text in Paul’s Epistle to the Hebrews (there is only one) there are other possibilities. Stephen could be reacting to Bloom’s preaching at him as saying what is written in verse five, “And again, I will be to him [Stephen] a Father, and he shall be to me a Son.” Verse nine contains words that Bloom might suggest apply to Stephen and his talents: “God, hath anointed thee… above thy fellows.” As for opening one’s mouth and putting one’s foot therein, in this context, it could be an indication of Stephen’s doubts over either assertion.
